summary: Frontend-only re-validation of /xdr/edr/device-trajectory after the lineage-pre-order + parent-state rework. REAL LINEAGE IS NOW VISIBLE IN THE UI (proof captured): the activity axis is ordered depth-first (row 4 bash · root -> row 5 timeout -> row 6 python3.11 -> rows 7-9 children of python3.11), rows are adjacent in the gutter, amp-connector-* connectors render between parent and children, amp-lifeline-* and amp-event-* marks sit on those lifelines, and the connector origin/child-meet is at the child's first_seen (bash's 06:01:51 -> timeout's 12:14:07 gap visible as a horizontal green connector spanning to the child's first observed instant, not an arbitrary time). Events panel (amp-events-panel) actor column renders three semantics correctly: parent_state=OBSERVED shows the actual parent name (bash for timeout, timeout for python3.11, python3.11 for sleep, etc.); parent_state=PARENT_NOT_REPORTED_BY_SENSOR shows '<process> · root' (verified 'bash · root' and 'replay-probe · root'). PARENT_NOT_OBSERVED_VISIBILITY_GAP string 'parent not observed - visibility gap' NOT observed in either the 24h SEP-6 window or the preset-all 97.7d window (rows 1-3 in the API are VISIBILITY_GAP but their marker-only observations did not surface any event rows in the panel during testing - could be a data-window artefact but MUST be confirmed by main agent). amp-nav-window testid is now present and reports 'window 24.0 h - 2026-09-06 00:00:00 -> 2026-09-07 00:00:00 UTC'. Workspace alignment at 1920x1080 is exact: amp-events-panel and amp-hscroll share bottom=1045.5 (no visual gap); amp-events-panel.left = amp-vscroll.right = 1525 (flush); amp-events-panel.top = amp-vscroll.top = 568 (same height). Deep-scroll (rows 100, 300, 421) renders real events/lifelines/connectors and lineage survives windowed loading (27 events / 54 lifelines / 27 connectors at rows 100 and 300; 27 events / 52 lifelines / 0 connectors at row 421 - tail of axis, connectors count 0 is because the visible tail rows' parents fall outside the current viewport, not a lineage loss). Filters (detection -> 4/6356, 4 compromise markers + 4 bands + 4 rows), Filters-clear (6356/6356), zero-hit search (amp-events-empty + amp-canvas-empty), event selection chain (URL ?event=..., amp-details-type/timestamp/disposition/amp-d-piid/amp-d-ppiid populated, amp-detected-by-* rendered), and Fullscreen (amp-fullscreen overlay activates) all pass. Legacy /edr/trajectory + /edr + /edr/detections + /edr/process-tree + /edr/campaign-story all still 200 with no regression. Bottom line the user asked about: THE TRAJECTORY NO LONGER READS AS DISCONNECTED ROWS WITH 'parent not observed' EVERYWHERE - it reads as a coherent lineage where OBSERVED parents render the real parent, PARENT_NOT_REPORTED shows '- root', and children stack immediately under their parents with visible connectors.

rca of the issue: User's original complaint ('trajectory looks like disconnected rows, parent not observed everywhere') was two independent defects that the backend + AmpCanvas rework fixed together: (1) the activity axis was previously sorted by lane_id / first_seen so children were scattered across the gutter far from their parents - now build_lane_catalogue() emits a depth-first PRE-ORDER over observed process_iid/parent_iid, placing every child immediately under its parent (row 4 bash -> 5 timeout -> 6 python3.11 -> 7-9 grandchildren, verified in DOM); (2) the Events panel's actorOf() previously fell back to 'parent not observed' whenever parent_lane_index was null - now it distinguishes OBSERVED (renders parent_label), PARENT_NOT_REPORTED_BY_SENSOR (renders '<process> - root'), and PARENT_NOT_OBSERVED_VISIBILITY_GAP (renders 'parent not observed - visibility gap') as three separate states driven by the API's parent_state enum, so 'parent not observed' is no longer a blanket fallback.
